notes: Exercise technique and compensation fields are educational biomechanical guidance, not a medical diagnosis.
The dataset is a curated/synthesized v1 and should undergo expert review before being used for automated high-stakes coaching.
Public ExerciseDB-derived data were used only as a schema/scale benchmark; this bundle does not reproduce its copyrighted media or verbatim instructions.
Cardio/conditioning is modeled as a first-class category with modality, protocol, intensity, impact, equipment, physiological demand, technique, warm-up and cooldown fields.

strength_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Shoulder horizontal adduction/flexion with elbow extension. Keep the movement controlled and repeatable for the selected variation. Finish each repetition under control and return to the start without a sudden drop.
strength_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Shoulders shrugging/protracting under load; elbows flaring excessively; loss of rib/pelvis control; bouncing or shortening the range without a reason
strength_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: Excess shoulder/anterior-deltoid or upper-trap contribution can rise when the scapula or ribcage is poorly controlled; the intended chest/triceps contribution may fall.
strength_conditioning.Correction Cue: Set a stable base; brace gently; control the eccentric; keep the forearm reasonably stacked over the hand; press through a consistent path.
strength_conditioning.Safety Notes: Use a load and range you can control. For free-weight presses, use a rack/safety pins or a spotter when appropriate.
strength_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: Band/cable press at low load; scapular push-up; 1–3 progressive ramp-up sets
strength_conditioning.Post-workout / Mobility Suggestion: Doorway pec stretch or gentle cross-body shoulder stretch

strength_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Shoulder extension/horizontal abduction with elbow flexion. Keep the movement controlled and repeatable for the selected variation. Finish each repetition under control and return to the start without a sudden drop.
strength_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Shrugging toward ears; pulling with the hands only; excessive lumbar extension; head jutting forward; uncontrolled release
strength_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: Upper-trap/arm-dominant pulling can replace cleaner scapular and lat/rhomboid contribution when the shoulder blade or trunk is poorly controlled.
strength_conditioning.Correction Cue: Keep ribs stacked; initiate with the shoulder blade; drive the elbow along the intended path; pause briefly without jerking.
strength_conditioning.Safety Notes: Do not force shoulder range or use momentum to overcome a sticking point.
strength_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: Band row; scapular retraction/depression drills; 1–2 light sets

strength_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: Back/upper-trap or knee demand may rise when the hip hinge is poorly coordinated; exact changes depend on the variation and person.
strength_conditioning.Correction Cue: Push hips back; keep load close; brace before moving; finish tall without leaning back; control the eccentric.
strength_conditioning.Safety Notes: Start with a load that allows repeatable spinal and hip control; learn the hinge before heavy loading.
strength_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: Dowel hinge; bodyweight RDL; glute bridge; ramp-up sets
strength_conditioning.Post-workout / Mobility Suggestion: Hamstring or hip-flexor stretch as individually appropriate

strength_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Hip flexion/extension with relatively stable knee angle and trunk bracing. Keep the pelvis and ribcage square and resist unwanted rotation. Finish each repetition under control and return to the start without a sudden drop.
strength_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Rounding or overextending the spine; turning a hinge into a squat; bar/load drifting far away; yanking the weight; losing foot pressure
strength_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: Back/upper-trap or knee demand may rise when the hip hinge is poorly coordinated; exact changes depend on the variation and person.
strength_conditioning.Correction Cue: Push hips back; keep load close; brace before moving; finish tall without leaning back; control the eccentric.
strength_conditioning.Safety Notes: Start with a load that allows repeatable spinal and hip control; learn the hinge before heavy loading.
strength_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: Dowel hinge; bodyweight RDL; glute bridge; ramp-up sets
strength_conditioning.Post-workout / Mobility Suggestion: Hamstring or hip-flexor stretch as individually appropriate

strength_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: Back/upper-trap or knee demand may rise when the hip hinge is poorly coordinated; exact changes depend on the variation and person.
strength_conditioning.Correction Cue: Push hips back; keep load close; brace before moving; finish tall without leaning back; control the eccentric.
strength_conditioning.Safety Notes: Start with a load that allows repeatable spinal and hip control; learn the hinge before heavy loading.
strength_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: Dowel hinge; bodyweight RDL; glute bridge; ramp-up sets
strength_conditioning.Post-workout / Mobility Suggestion: Hamstring or hip-flexor stretch as individually appropriate

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Strength vs hypertrophy vs power vs endurance vs mobility/general fitness
programming_rules.Practical implication: Match exercise resistance profile, skill demand, fatigue cost and progression potential to the goal.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Heavier loads can improve strength; complete ROM and technique matter
programming_rules.Practical implication: Prioritize stable, skill-appropriate compound patterns; put high-priority strength work early.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Sufficient weekly volume is a major driver; many loads can work
programming_rules.Practical implication: Prefer exercises that can be executed consistently and progressed without excessive fatigue or pain.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Moderate loads and fast concentric intent
programming_rules.Practical implication: Use explosive variants only when technique/readiness support them; stop sets before speed/technique collapse.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: General preparation + movement-specific rehearsal + ramp sets
programming_rules.Practical implication: Use dynamic movement preparation and low-fatigue rehearsal; warm-up should improve readiness, not create fatigue.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Static stretching is not mandatory for every session; dynamic preparation can fit warm-up
programming_rules.Practical implication: Use the type of mobility/stretching that matches the immediate task and individual ROM needs.
Prioritize key patterns early, then accessories and less technically demanding work.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: No equipment, dumbbells, bands, kettlebells, machines, cables, full gym
programming_rules.Practical implication: Filter impossible choices first, then score the remaining movements by muscle/goal fit.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Watch for loss of foot pressure, trunk position, joint tracking, range control, speed or tempo
programming_rules.Practical implication: Regress load, ROM, complexity, assistance or implement before prescribing more volume.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Poor technique may redistribute demand, but the change is individual
programming_rules.Practical implication: Use 'may increase demand' rather than claiming a guaranteed wrong-muscle diagnosis.

programming_rules.What the AI should consider: Load, reps, ROM, lever, stability and complexity can be progressed
programming_rules.Practical implication: Change one or two variables at a time while maintaining repeatable technique.
Treat corrective exercise as a movement-improvement workflow, not a diagnosis engine.

cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.
cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.

cardio_conditioning.Effort Guidance: Repeated hard bouts with planned recovery
cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.
cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.

cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.

cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.
cardio_conditioning.Best-Fit Goal: cardiorespiratory fitness; conditioning; calorie expenditure; endurance
cardio_conditioning.Evidence Level: High for general aerobic exercise principles; modality-specific technique varies
cardio_conditioning.Source / Method: ACSM / WHO / AHA aerobic exercise principles + NSCA conditioning framework

cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.
cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.

cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.

cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.
cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.

cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.

cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.

cardio_conditioning.Execution / Form Cues: Use a repeatable technique and posture appropriate to the modality. Start at a sustainable intensity, control breathing, and increase pace or resistance progressively.
cardio_conditioning.Common Posture/Technique Errors: Starting too hard; losing posture as fatigue rises; excessive gripping or shoulder tension; compensating with uncontrolled spinal motion; ignoring cadence or resistance control.
cardio_conditioning.Likely Compensation / Demand Shift: As technique degrades, local muscles may fatigue inefficiently and stress can shift toward joints or non-target regions; the intended aerobic workload may become less efficient.
cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.

cardio_conditioning.Correction Cue: Reduce pace or resistance until technique is repeatable; restore neutral, controlled posture; relax unnecessary tension; then progress intensity gradually.
cardio_conditioning.Warm-up Preparation: 5–10 minutes easy modality-specific movement plus progressive ramps; use dynamic mobility relevant to the joints being used.
cardio_conditioning.Cooldown / Recovery: 5–10 minutes easy movement followed by optional comfortable mobility work; rehydrate as appropriate.
cardio_conditioning.Safety Notes: Stop for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, faintness or other concerning symptoms. Progress impact and intensity gradually, especially for new trainees.
cardio_conditioning.Best-Fit Goal: cardiorespiratory fitness; conditioning; calorie expenditure; endurance
cardio_conditioning.Evidence Level: High for general aerobic exercise principles; modality-specific technique varies
cardio_conditioning.Source / Method: ACSM / WHO / AHA aerobic exercise principles + NSCA conditioning framework
